title: Ames on faith of special mercy: unto Christ before justification — of mercy already given after
source_text: XLVIII. Quibus consentanea docet idem Amesius in Bellarmino Enervato; ubi observat fidem specialis misericordiae duplici ratione sic vocari. Primo qua Christum apprehendit, vel innititur ipsi, ad specialem misericordiam per ipsum apprehendendam: Secundo qua misericordiam specialem, ut jam donatam, apprehendit. Et priore sensu dicit fidem specialis misericordiae antecedere justificationem, & maxime proprie dici justificare: fidem vero specialis misericordiae, posteriore sensu, sequi justificationem, nec eo respectu nos per eam justificari. Ibidem vero verbis Cardinalis Contareni explicat quid significet per apprehensionem illam qua Christum apprehendimus, & ipsi innitimur, ad specialem misericordiam per ipsum apprehendendam: Nempe non illam apprehensionem quae pertinet ad cognitionem intellectus; sed qua dicimur illud apprehendere quo pervenimus, & quod post motum nostrum attingimus. Et subjungit fidem justificantem a multis tamen Theologis describi per posteriorem illum fidei actum, quo certi reddimur de impetrata & donata nobis Dei in Christo misericordia.
pass_a_gloss: Things agreeable to these the same Ames teaches in Bellarmine Enervated; where he observes that faith of special mercy is so called in a twofold way. First as that by which it apprehends Christ, or leans on Him, unto special mercy to be apprehended through Him: Second as that by which it apprehends special mercy as already given. And in the former sense he says faith of special mercy precedes justification, and is most properly said to justify: but faith of special mercy in the latter sense follows justification, and in that respect we are not justified by it. And there by the words of Cardinal Contarini he explains what he means by that apprehension by which we apprehend Christ and lean on Him unto special mercy to be apprehended through Him: Namely not that apprehension which pertains to the cognition of the intellect; but that by which we are said to apprehend that to which we arrive, and which we reach after our motion. And he subjoins that justifying faith is nevertheless described by many Theologians through that latter act of faith by which we are made sure of God's mercy in Christ obtained and given to us.
pass_b_english: Ames (Bell. Enerv.): ‘faith of special mercy’ in two senses.
1. Apprehend/lean on Christ unto mercy through Him — precedes justification; most properly justifies.
2. Apprehend mercy as already given — follows justification; does not justify in that respect.
Apprehension = arriving/reaching Christ, not bare intellect-grasp.
Many still describe justifying faith by the latter assurance-act.
